purpose: Append an immutable resolution event for an original-terms continuing obligation without deleting, replacing or mutating prior lifecycle observations or the closed source engagement.

field_rules.predecessor_state: Must name the authentically observed lifecycle state immediately preceding this resolution event.
field_rules.predecessor_observation_ref: Must identify the retained predecessor observation/receipt; it is never overwritten.
field_rules.triggering_evidence_refs: Exact evidence that justifies this resolution observation.
field_rules.resolution_actor: Accountable obligation owner or counterpart/waiving party as required by the resolution semantics.
field_rules.actor_authority_evidence_refs: Required when the resolution depends on authority, especially WAIVED; may be an empty array only when the resolution is purely evidence-of-performance and no counterpart/waiver authority is required.
field_rules.resulting_state: SATISFIED, WAIVED or BREACHED_OR_UNSATISFIED for ordinary resolution receipts; CURE_SATISFIED or CURE_WAIVED for append-only later cure/waiver receipts.

WAIVED: waiving party identity and authority evidence

cure.rule: A later cure never edits or supersedes a BREACHED_OR_UNSATISFIED receipt. Append a new cure receipt referencing the prior unsatisfied receipt and new cure evidence.
cure.projection_rule: A current-state projection may report SATISFIED_AFTER_CURE or WAIVED_AFTER_UNSATISFIED while reconstruction must retain the earlier BREACHED_OR_UNSATISFIED event and every intervening observation.

append_only_history.rule: Resolution receipts form an ordered evidence history by predecessor reference and timestamp. No receipt deletes, edits, replaces or retroactively changes an earlier observation.
append_only_history.projection_boundary: Receipt timestamp/order does not establish validity. Projection requires authentic predecessor/evidence/authority relationships and a unique valid frontier.

legal_boundary: Receipts record evidence dispositions only and do not establish legal breach, damages, default, enforceability, remedy, release or discharge.
